title: India Launches UPI Tap-and-Pay Ahead of Full Apple Pay Rollout
excerpt: The NFC-based UPI feature works even without a network connection and lands weeks before Apple's expected full India launch — while NPCI quietly prepares AI agents that can pay on your behalf.
body:
• India's National Payments Corporation of India launched a tap-and-pay feature for UPI on Thursday, letting users pay by tapping their phone at a terminal without opening a payments app.
  • The NFC-based feature is designed to work in areas with little or no network connectivity, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra and NPCI chairman Ajay Kumar Choudhary announced at the Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai.
  • The launch comes ahead of an expected full Apple Pay rollout in India by October; a beta version of Apple's service has been available for some time.
  • UPI remains the world's largest retail fast-payment system by volume, processing 24.51 billion transactions worth ₹29.82 lakh crore ($314.21 billion) in August alone.

India launched a tap-and-pay option for its real-time payments network on Thursday, letting shoppers complete transactions by tapping their smartphones at point-of-sale terminals without opening the UPI app. The move arrives weeks ahead of an expected full launch of Apple Pay in India.

The feature was unveiled at the Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai, where NPCI non-executive chairman Ajay Kumar Choudhary said it uses near-field communication (NFC) technology and is designed to work in areas with little or no network connectivity. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra, who launched UPI Tap & Pay alongside the AI-powered MyUPI platform and a framework for corporate bond tokenisation, framed the announcements as the next phase of India's digital finance expansion.

Context & Background

The Unified Payments Interface, operated by the National Payments Corporation of India, is the world's largest retail fast-payment system by transaction volume, according to a 2025 IMF report. In August alone it processed 24.51 billion transactions worth ₹29.82 lakh crore — about $314.21 billion. UPI's success rests on instant settlement, interoperability across hundreds of banks and apps, and near-zero merchant fees, which made QR-code payments ubiquitous from street vendors to large retailers.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=eakngayy0V0

Apple's relationship with Indian payments has been incremental. A beta version of Apple Pay has been available in India for some time, but a full launch is expected by October, according to local media reports cited by Reuters. By putting tap-to-pay on UPI itself, NPCI ensures the homegrown rails — not a foreign wallet — define the experience when Apple's rollout lands.

Impact & Analysis

Tap-to-pay matters because of where India's digital payments are weakest. QR-code UPI depends on a working data connection and an opened app; in patchy-network areas, transactions still fail. An NFC tap that works offline removes both frictions and brings UPI closer to the speed of a card tap in the West. For merchants, faster checkout at busy counters could widen acceptance further into the small-ticket retail that already dominates UPI volumes.

The timing is strategic. Apple Pay's full entry would introduce tokenised card payments and wallet-based NFC on iPhones — the first genuine competition for UPI at the tap terminal. Launching UPI's own tap-and-pay first keeps the public rails in front of the private wallet, preserving NPCI's hold on how India pays at the counter. It also deepens the contrast with card networks: UPI's 640 million daily transactions already rival Visa's global daily volumes, according to Indian government data.

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora, UPI's tap-and-pay and the coming Apple Pay rollout change the travel math. NRIs visiting India have long juggled foreign cards, forex markups, and clunky app setups; a tap-enabled UPI — with international wallet access already extended through schemes like UPI One World for visitors — makes paying in India feel closer to home-country convenience. If Apple's October launch brings iPhone-native UPI payments, diaspora users may finally tap the same way abroad and in India.

What's Next

NPCI's ambitions extend well beyond taps. Reuters reported that the payments authority is building a registry to verify and monitor AI agents making payments on UPI — part of a planned Unified Agentic Protocol that would let artificial intelligence agents make small, frequent purchases, like groceries, without users approving each transaction. The registry would initially vet agents on UPI and could later cover cards and bill payments, with spending limits, audit trails, and identity checks built in. Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and China's payments body are all building similar agent registries. Between tap-and-pay today and agentic payments tomorrow, India's payments roadmap is moving faster than anyone else's — and the rest of the world is now racing to keep up.
nri_angle: Tap-enabled UPI plus an October Apple Pay launch make paying in India far easier for NRIs visiting home, potentially matching the tap convenience they have abroad.
author: Diaspora Desk
